statement.p: Integrate f(x,y,z)=18 xz over the region in the first octant (x,y,z\ge 0) above the parabolic cylinder z=y^2 and below the paraboloid z=8-2x^2-y^2.

static.solution:
\mathcal{W} onto the xy-plane. We find the curve of intersection between the upper and lower surfaces,
by solving the following equation for x,y\ge 0: 8-2{x}^2-{y}^2={y}^2\quad \Rightarrow\quad {y}^2=4-{x}^2\quad \Rightarrow\quad y=\sqrt{4-{x}^2}, x\ge 0 The projection \mathcal{D} of \mathcal{W} onto the xy-plane is the region bounded by the circle {x}^2+{y}^2=4 and the positive axes.
We now compute the triple integral over \mathcal{W} by evaluating the following iterated integral:
\begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 18 xz \,dV \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} \left(\int_{{y}^2}^{8-2{x}^2-{y}^2}18 xz \,dz\right)\,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 9xz^2\bigg|_{{z=y}^2}^{8-2{x}^2-{y}^2}dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 9x\left({\left(8-2{x}^2-{y}^2\right)}^2-{y}^4\right) \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}}9x\left(8-2{x}^2-2{y}^2\right)\left(8-2{x}^2\right)\,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 36x\left(4-{x}^2\right)\left(4-{x}^2-{y}^2\right) \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^2 \left(36x\left(4-{x}^2\right) \int_0^{\sqrt{4-{x}^2}} \left(4-{x}^2-{y}^2\right) \,dy\right)dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^2 36x\left(4-{x}^2\right)\left(\left(4-{x}^2\right)y-\frac{{y}^3}{3}\right)\bigg|_{y=0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^2}} \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^2 36x\left(4-{x}^2\right)\left({\left(4-{x}^2\right)}^{3/2}-\frac{{\left(4-{x}^2\right)}^{3/2}}{3}\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^2 \frac{72}{3}{\left(4-{x}^2\right)}^{5/2}x \,dx \end{array} We compute the integral using the substitution u=4-{x}^2, du=-2x \,dx. This gives
\begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 18 xz \,dV \amp =\amp \int_0^2 \frac{72}{3}{\left(4-{x}^2\right)}^{5/2}x \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_4^0 \frac{72}{3}{u}^{5/2}\left(-\frac{du}{2}\right)= \int_0^4 \frac{36}{3}{u}^{5/2} \,du\\ \amp =\amp \frac{36}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{7}{u}^{7/2}\bigg|_0^4= \frac{72}{21}\cdot {4}^{7/2}\\ \amp =\amp \frac{72}{21}\cdot 2^7= \frac{9216}{21}\approx 438.857 \end{array}
